summary: Loaded the newest durable Macro receipt, validated the Hybrid registry/contract and missing request pointers, screened fresh global macro/rates/FX/commodity evidence, and identified one material policy-regime change. The Reserve Bank of India raised the repo rate 25 basis points to 5.50%, its first increase in nearly four years, and changed its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening. The rate size was largely priced, but the stance shift was the material surprise. Immediate reaction was contained in Indian bonds, INR and rate-sensitive equities. ORACLE promotes an RBI calibrated-tightening regime but not a global crisis state; SUPERMESH-X records two reporting origins, the expectation baseline and the unavailable direct RBI release.
